item.title: Calvin football stuns Hope for historic first win in The Rivalry to clinch MIAA title share
item.description: GRAND RAPIDS - The Rivalry has been the best NCAA Division III basketball rivalry in the country for more than a century. Football has joined The Rivalry for the first time. Sure it is the third game that Hope and Calvin have played, but with the Knights starting a program just three years ago, it took a couple years to get up to speed, and get a home stadium. Both teams came into the clash undefeated and tied for first place in the MIAA and the game lived up to the anticipation. Tied to start the fourth quarter, Calvin's Luke Michmerhuizen caught two long touchdown passes the Knights hung on for their first win in the rivalry 38-24 on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Calvin's brand-new Knight Stadium. The Knights improved to 9-0 and 6-0 in the MIAA, clinching a share of the league title. Hope dropped to 8-1 and 5-1 in the MIAA. Hope can clinch a share with a win over Trine and a Calvin loss to Alma next week, but the Knights would have the tiebreaker for the automatic bit to the NCAA tournament. Hope had outscored Calvin 90-7 through the first to matchups. The Knights took their first lead ever over Hope in the second quarter when Luke Michmerhuizen caught a pass from Thomas Vaccaro with 8:31 to go in the half 14-10. After a 42-yard Hope touchdown pass from Alex Thole to Trevor Griffiths, Calvin marched down the field again and scored on a Vaccaro scramble up the middle for a 21-17 Calvin lead at halftime. Alex Thole scored on a quarterback keeper with 3:30 to go in the third quarter, tying it 24-24. Michmerhuizen snagged a 39-yard touchdown catch down the sideline, leaping to grab it at the goal line with 6:59 to go for a 31-24 lead. Calvin tried an onside kick and it went out of bounds for a penalty. Hope got the ball in Calvin territory but couldn't get anything going and punted it back to the Knights with 5:45 to go. Three plays later, Michmerhuizen caught another long touchdown pass, this one from 64-yards out to make it 38-24. This is a developing story and will be updated as details and reaction unfold. item.title: Almirón’s $15,000 Gift Shows Atlanta United’s Real Heart
item.description: Mark Smith-Imagn Images Miguel Almirón proved that true leadership goes far beyond the scoreboard on Thursday. The Atlanta United captain accepted the 2026 Media Ambassador Award and immediately pledged the $5,000 cash prize to a local charity. He did not stop there. The club matched his gift with another $10,000, bringing the total support for the Agape Youth and Family Center to $15,000. This move highlights a team that cares about its community even as its season struggles. While the money matters, the words spoken by Almirón carry even more weight. He explained his drive to help during a media session at the Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta Training Ground. “Whenever it’s within our reach, you have to help,” Almirón said in Spanish Thursday, according to Atlanta United FC . He spoke from personal experience, noting that his own family found opportunity through football after moving to the United States. The donation targets a non-profit with a clear mission to end generational poverty for underserved families. Almirón visited the center last year and saw the need with his own eyes. Injury Woes Mount Before Decision Day The on-field product faces a much harder test than the off-field goodwill. The roster is thin heading into the final match against Red Bull New York. Atlanta United lists Will Reilly as out due to an ankle injury. The team faces a long list of absent players across the league. Charlotte FC will miss Nimfasha Berchimas, Will Cleary, Archie Goodwin, Aron John, and Tim Ream. Chicago Fire FC loses Robin Lod and Sam Rogers to lower body issues. FC Cincinnati has Nick Hagglund in concussion protocol. The depth of these losses is staggering for a team trying to find momentum. Atlanta United’s head coach Tata Martino sees a path forward despite the bad luck. He believes the team is building the right habits for the next season. “We have shown an attitude and willingness that is essentially focused on the future rather than what is happening right now,” head coach Tata Martino said in Spanish Thursday. The coach added that this mindset is crucial for the players. “We need that in order to believe in what’s coming.” The 4 p.m. ET kickoff on Saturday will not decide playoff spots, but it will show if the squad can finish strong. Atlanta Supporters Deserve Wins Almirón acknowledges the gap between where the team is and where it needs to be. He admitted the campaign has been frustrating for everyone involved. item.title: Bengals-Falcons by the numbers/overseas games
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals head to Madrid to face the Atlanta Falcons in Week 9 and are still seeking their first win overseas. The Bengals have played twice overseas – both at Wembley Stadium in London – and have a loss and tie. Cincinnati (5-2) is coming off a win over the Tennessee Titans and Atlanta (3-5) is coming off a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8. Can the Bengals get their first win overseas and also be the first NFL team to win a showcase game in Madrid? Here's what the numbers say: Bengals overseas record The first time the Bengals played overseas was in 2016 against the Washington Commanders. The game ended in a 27-27 tie. The last time the Bengals were overseas was Zac Taylor's first season as head coach and Cincinnati lost 24-10 to the Los Angeles Rams . The Bengals would eventually meet the Rams in Super Bowl 56, suffering a 23-20 loss. Falcons overseas record The Falcons have played one more game than the Bengals abroad and have a win as well. Atlanta's first game was a 21-20 loss to the Detroit Lions at Wembley Stadium in 2014, which was followed by a 27-20 win over the New York Jets at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London in 2021. The Falcons most recently had a 23-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2023. Bengals vs. Falcons all-time record The Bengals lead the all-time series against the Falcons at 10-5. The two teams most recently met Oct. 23, 2022 at Paycor Stadium and the Bengals won 35-17. The 2022 win made it a three-game winning streak for the Bengals against the Falcons. Bengals vs. Falcons most points scored The most points scored between the two teams in the history of the all-time series was in 2018 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The Bengals won 37-36 on a 16-yard touchdown pass from Andy Dalton to A.J. Green with 7 seconds remaining in the game to move to 3-1 on the season, but would eventually miss the playoffs. Dalton and Falcons quarterback Matt Ryan each threw three touchdowns in the game and combined to throw for more than 700 yards in the shootout. Bengals vs. Falcons first game The first game between the two franchises was Nov. 7, 1971 at Riverfront Stadium. The Falcons won 9-6 thanks to a fourth quarter touchdown pass from quarterback Dick Shiner to Art Malone. Shiner had 150 passing yards on the day and Bengals quarterback Virgil Carter was 10-for-24 passing for 88 yards and two interceptions. The Falcons rushing attack was led by Cannonball Butler who had 68 yards and the Bengals were led by Jess Phillips who had 63 rushing yards. The Bengals are 0-2 against the spread all time overseas while the Falcons are 2-1 against the number. item.title: Will Ryan Hopkins, Colton Joseph play for Wisconsin football vs Rutgers?
item.description: MADISON – Ryan Hopkins will officially get his first career start as Wisconsin football takes on Rutgers on Nov. 7. UW coach Luke Fickell confirmed as much in his pregame interview with the Badger Radio Network . Hopkins might not be the only quarterback to see the field, though. "I just think we got to get in a rhythm,” Fickell told radio commentator Mark Tauscher. “I think that we got to continue to have balance. We could see both of them. Colton is up and ready to roll, but Ryan's going to get the opportunity to lead the offense.” CBS Sports and On3 first reported Hopkins’ expected start on Nov. 6. The freshman quarterback replaced Colton Joseph – UW’s presumed starter since transferring in January – late in the third quarter of the 30-0 loss to Iowa . The CBS report said that Joseph has been “dealing with an injury.” However, Joseph did not have any designation on Wisconsin ’s pregame availability reports on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday. Fickell downplayed a question at his Nov. 2 press conference about knowing who the starting quarterback was going to be, saying that “this isn’t what this is about” and Hopkins’ opportunity was “just based on where we were in the situation of the game.” Joseph has completed 55.6% of his passes while throwing for 1,346 yards and rushing for 371 yards through the Badgers ’ first eight games. His 130.1 passer rating ranks 92nd among 124 qualifying FBS quarterbacks. Hopkins, who quickly ascended the depth chart in spring practices and fall camp, threw for 93 yards on 8-of-13 passing against the Hawkeyes. “This is all about growing and getting better,” Fickell said in the pregame radio interview. item.title: 3 takeaways from Iowa State football's loss vs Baylor | Hines
item.description: WACO, Texas – For the fourth consecutive drive, the Iowa State football defense – swarming, imposing and physical – forced Baylor 's offense – rudderless, listless and limping – to punt the ball away. And the entire game changed. A muffed punt gave the ball back to Baylor, and the Bears seemingly never stopped scoring from there to defeat the Cyclones, 42-31 , on Nov. 7 at McLane Stadium. In a season that has not been short on frustration, this may be the most vexing loss of the year for the Cyclones (4-5, 2-4 Big 12). Through a quarter-and-a-half, Iowa State was the vastly superior team with Aiden Flora running wild on offense and the Cyclone defense handcuffing the Baylor attack. Then Flora, for the second time this season, failed to cleanly field the punt, and Baylor recovered near midfield. Two plays later, the Bears were in the endzone. The Bears would score touchdowns on three straight possessions and six of eight to take a commanding lead that they would not relinquish. Iowa State remains winless away from Jack Trice Stadium this season, and the Cyclones remain two victories shy of bowl eligibility with three games to play. Here are three takeaways from Saturday's loss to Baylor. Defensive collapse Through its first four drives of the game, the Baylor offense managed just 46 yards. Quarterback DJ Lagway looked hurried and bothered, and the Bears punted on each possession, managing just three first downs along the way. Their next three drives to end the first half went 48 yards, 75 yards and 78 yards, all resulting in touchdowns. It was as swift and dramatic a defensive collapse as you could imagine. While Iowa State's offense has drawn considerable criticism this season, the defense has simply not been up to the task in Big 12 play. That's three straight games in which they've surrendered at least 35 points. The only time the Cyclones have kept an opponent under 30 points was in a 24-10 loss to BYU, in which the Cougars turned it over on downs multiple times inside the red zone. Iowa State's defense began the year very openly setting its expectations for itself very high, hoping to keep opponents to 14 points or below. The Cyclones have come nowhere near meeting their own standard in Big 12 play. More: Iowa State vs Baylor football live updates: Bears score late touchdown Flora piles up yardage The muffed point absolutely changed the game for Iowa State, and it'll likely overshadow what was otherwise an excellent offensive game from Flora. The ADM graduate rushed 26 times for 182 yards and a score to continue what has been an incredible breakout season. For as much as Iowa State's offense has struggled at times and for how many questions there will be about how to fill out the roster in 2027, Flora's emergence as a true star gives the Cyclones not only a chance in their three remaining games, but a player to build around going forward. item.title: Toto Wolff explains the emotional Mercedes factory email leaked online
item.description: Motorsport photo Securing a Formula 1 world championship triggers a lot of emotions, and, usually, a lot of champagne. But for Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, Kimi Antonelli's historic title win in Mexico City triggered a sudden urge to write an incredibly long essay to his staff. During the Free Practice 3 broadcast at the Brazilian Grand Prix, Sky Sports F1 presenter Simon Lazenby brought up a rather inspiring internal Mercedes email that recently made its way onto the internet. Wolff, in classic deadpan fashion, immediately roasted the broadcaster for actually taking the time to read the whole thing. "Did you read such a long email? It was quite long," Wolff joked. When Lazenby confirmed he read it all the way through, Wolff fired back, "I was surprised the last time I wrote it [something that long] was under severe pressure in school." Deflecting the spotlight Jokes aside, Wolff explained the emotional catalyst behind the massive message. As the guy who officially signed off on putting a teenager into Lewis Hamilton's legendary seat, Wolff was getting flooded with congratulatory messages from the media and the paddock. He didn't want it. "So why was it spontaneous? Because I got so much praise on that Sunday night about giving him the opportunity and in Italy," Wolff explained to the Sky Sports crew. "And it's something that makes you very proud. But I felt I needed to give credit to all the people that maybe weren't so much in the spotlight." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Formula 1 is the ultimate team sport, and pushing a rookie through a brutal 2025 slump to a 2026 World Championship took an entire village of engineers, strategists, and mentors. Wolff wanted to make sure the men and women turning the wrenches and crunching the data knew this was their trophy, too. "This email, he didn't even give it justice because there is many more that were part of the decision-making process and getting him to where he was," the Mercedes boss continued. "And that's why I felt like I need to at least express my gratitude to the big team." The LinkedIn leak So how did a private, internal factory memo end up public? You can thank Mercedes communications boss and senior leadership figure Bradley Lord for that. When Wolff hit send on his emotional late-night draft, Lord apparently decided the message was far too good to keep locked inside the company inbox. Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal "And then Bradley felt that was a more clever email than normally," Wolff laughed. "So he put it on LinkedIn, and that it was when it was spread." It might have been an accidental public relations masterclass, but it offered fans a rare, unscripted look at the nurturing culture Wolff has built inside the Mercedes garage. item.title: Orsolini praise for Bologna coach Palladino is damning for Tedesco
item.description: Orsolini praise for Bologna coach Palladino is damning for Tedesco Bologna won their fourth game in a row under new coach Raffaele Palladino, as Riccardo Orsolini pins the blame on sacked Domenico Tedesco. ‘We’re enjoying ourselves again.’ The Rossoblu had got off to a truly disastrous start under former Belgium international coach Tedesco, scraping one point from the opening four Serie A matches. All three defeats were 1-0 scorelines, and he was fired on September 16 to bring in Palladino. It has been a complete transformation, drawing the opener and then winning five of the next six games, faltering only 3-1 to Inter. Orsolini sees Bologna turnaround ITALY – NOVEMBER 07: Riccardo Orsolini of Bologna FC celebrates winning the match against Parma Calcio during the Serie A match between Parma Calcio and Bologna FC at Stadio Ennio Tardini on November 07, 2026 in Parma, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) “The coach arrived in a bit of a rush, because we had started so badly and there was no time to discuss too much,” Orsolini told DAZN Italia after today’s 2-1 win away to Parma , their fourth on the bounce. “We had to win games, he did well to get us all on the same page and bring us back together, seeing as this was a team that had done well over the years. We lost some important players over the summer, but the skeleton of that team remained.” When Orsolini had praise for Palladino, he namechecked several previous Bologna bosses too, but notably left Tedesco out of the list. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Raffaele Palladino Head Coach of Bologna FC looks on prior to the Serie A match between Bologna FC and AC Monza at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) “I’ve been here for many years and went through a lot of different situations. I enjoyed myself with Thiago Motta, with Vincenzo Italiano, and now we are enjoying ourselves again with Palladino. “I don’t know how far this team can go, but we want to enjoy ourselves together. We rediscovered our smile.” ITALY – SEPTEMBER 06: Domenico Tedesco manager of Bologna FC 1909 looks on during the Serie A match between Bologna FC and US Sassuolo at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on September 6, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Bologna are climbing back up the table after four consecutive victories against Cagliari, Milan, Monza and Parma, but notably three of those were away from home. This was Orsolini’s second goal of the season in just five appearances, as it was his comeback from almost a month out with a thigh injury.
